title: PSB Rc 10 (Pagsanjan) Rice Variety: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: PSB Rc 10 Rice Variety: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: PSB Rc 10 is an inbred rice for irrigated lowland: about 106 days and 4.8 tonnes per hectare on average. See its pest ratings and grain quality.
excerpt: PSB Rc 10 is an inbred rice variety for irrigated lowland, known locally as Pagsanjan. The Philippine Seed Board approved it in 1992. IRRI bred it. It matures in about 106 days and averages 4.8 tonnes per hectare, with a top yield of 7.5 tonnes in trials.

blocks.text: If you came here looking for rice variety 10, or Rc 10, this is the one. The facts below come from sources that include PhilRice and its public seed database. So you can compare it with the other varieties in our [rice variety finder](/rice-varieties) before you buy seed. Also read our guide to [rice varieties in the Philippines](/crops/rice-varieties-philippines) for how inbreds, hybrids and special rice differ.

items: **Yield:** 4.8 tonnes per hectare on average, or about 96 cavans of 50 kilograms. The best trial reached 7.5 tonnes.
**Holds up against:** rice blast, brown planthopper, green leafhopper.
**Cooked rice:** high amylose, so firm and fluffy.

blocks.text: How much does PSB Rc 10 yield?

On average it gives 4.8 tonnes per hectare. That is about 96 cavans of 50 kilograms of palay. It sits below the average of the 107 irrigated lowland inbreds in PhilRice's list, which is 5.1 tonnes. But the top yield, 7.5 tonnes, came from a trial with good water, seed and care. So plan your costs on the average, then work toward the top with the habits in our guide to [raising rice yield per hectare](/blog/increase-rice-yield-per-hectare).
How many days does it take to mature?

It takes about 106 days from sowing to harvest. IRRI groups varieties of 100 to 120 days as short duration and 120 to 140 days as medium, so this one counts as short duration. Then harvest when 85 to 90 percent of the grains turn golden yellow, as PalayCheck advises. Because the day count drives every task, anee.io counts it for you from each lot's own planting day, with the [growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.

blocks.text: It showed no weak spot in the ratings PhilRice lists. Still, a resistant variety can break down when a new strain of a disease or a new pest population comes. So keep scouting, and use our [pest and disease finders](/features/pest-and-disease-finders) when something looks wrong.

blocks.caption: Grain quality in PhilRice's seed database

blocks.text: Amylose decides how rice cooks. With high amylose, expect rice that is firm and dry, and it hardens as it cools. In fact, PhilRice notes that Filipino taste moved from high to intermediate and low amylose rice, because people want it softer. Head rice is the share of whole grains after milling. So a higher number means fewer broken grains and a better price at the mill.

It suits irrigated lowland, where you control the water. Level the field well so the water stands evenly, and plant at the same time as your neighbors, one of the PalayCheck key checks, so pests cannot move from field to field. Our guide to [rice land preparation](/land-preparation/rice-land-preparation) shows each step. PhilRice recommends it for the dry season and the wet season. You can plant it dry direct seeded, transplanted or wet direct seeded. It was tested and found suitable in Central Luzon. For the right month in your province, see [the best time to plant rice](/blog/best-time-to-plant-rice-philippines).

items.q: What is the local name of PSB Rc 10?
items.a: It is known as Pagsanjan. Seed sellers and agriculturists use both names, so ask for either one.

items.q: How many days does PSB Rc 10 take to harvest?
items.a: About 106 days after sowing. Then harvest when 85 to 90 percent of the grains are golden yellow.

items.q: What is the average yield of PSB Rc 10?
items.a: PhilRice lists 4.8 tonnes per hectare on average, about 96 cavans of 50 kilograms. The best trial reached 7.5 tonnes. Your own yield depends on water, seed, fertilizer and timing.

items.q: In which season should I plant it?
